notes.translatedIn: NAT outside→inside: the destination {{from}} becomes {{to}} again.
notes.translatedError: NAT outside→inside: this ICMP error is about {{from}}; it goes to the inside host {{to}}.
notes.created: NAT has no translation for {{local}} yet: access list {{acl}} selects it, so a new entry maps it to {{global}}.
notes.poolExhausted: NAT access list {{acl}} selects {{local}}, but no address or port is free: the packet is dropped and ICMP host unreachable goes back.
notes.noAddress: NAT should use the address of {{iface}}, which has none: the packet leaves untranslated.
notes.notSelected: No NAT rule selects {{src}}: the packet leaves untranslated.
notes.protocolNotTranslated: NAT overload translates only ICMP, TCP and UDP: this packet leaves untranslated.
notes.noTranslation: {{dst}} is a NAT address but no translation exists for this packet: it is dropped.

form.rolesHint: Mark the LAN ports “Inside” and the WAN port “Outside” in the port editor (NAT role). Only packets that go from an inside to an outside port are translated.
form.rulesHint: Inside addresses that the access list permits are translated to the pool or to the interface address. Overload (PAT) lets many inside hosts share one address by port.
form.overloadHint: Share the address between hosts by port number.
form.staticsHint: A fixed inside ↔ outside pair, so the outside can reach an inside host. Choose TCP or UDP to forward one port only.

errors.endBeforeStart: The last address comes before the first one.
errors.differentSubnets: The first and last address must be in the same subnet of this netmask.
errors.duplicateStatic: This inside address already has a mapping.
errors.unknownPool: Choose a pool of this list.
errors.duplicateRule: Another rule uses this access list.
